rule_applied.decision_use: informs framing only; feeds pivot rule 'Reframe the whole project'

verdict_basis: area recall = 10 m scar-component px that are also positive under the 20 m rule / 10 m scar-component px, point estimate (yaml method.proposed_not_in_memo.area_recall)

scar.definition: largest 8-connected 10 m parent-positive component within plausibility_radius_m = 1500 of the crown (configs/wayanad_evidence.yaml), as in the 2026-09-29 evidence run

validity_effect.note: sensitivity only: scar px whose 2 x 2 cell has an invalid child cannot be positive at 20 m

distance_to_published_points_m.definition: minimum distance from the point to the centre of any pixel of the component; published coordinates are a plausibility check, never a label

measurements.name: area_recall_20m_rule_vs_10m_scar
measurements.unit: fraction of the 10 m scar component area also positive under the 20 m rule
measurements.bootstrap_unit: 32 x 32 px (10 m) = 320 m tiles; the scar covers few tiles, so the CI is coarse

measurements.name: IoU_20m_scar_component_vs_10m_scar_component
measurements.unit: IoU after nearest-neighbour upsampling 20 m -> 10 m

measurements.name: IoU_20m_parent_mask_vs_10m_scar_component
measurements.unit: IoU of ALL 20 m positive cells (upsampled) vs the 10 m scar component; extra positives count against it

limitations: One scene, one event, one scar: this informs framing only (yaml: abandon_when "—"); it is not a generalisation about landslides.

The 10 m scar component is a threshold-0.30 NDVI-drop component (provisional, set before viewing data), not a surveyed polygon; recall is agreement with the 10 m rule, not accuracy against truth. No 2.5 m or 10 m change truth exists for Wayanad.

A 20 m cell is invalid if any child is invalid on any date, so cloud/shadow edges inside the scar cannot be positive at 20 m; validity_effect reports how many scar px that touches and the recall restricted to the rest.
Both rules use the single post date 2024-12-06 (129 days after the event); season and regrowth are confounded with the landslide at both resolutions.
The recall CI resamples 320 m tiles of one component and is coarse; the verdict uses the point estimate as pre-registered.

The prompt says "the component intersecting the published crown location"; the committed yaml says the largest component within 1500 m of the crown, which is what is used. The 10 m component lies 5.7 m from the crown point, so it does not strictly intersect it.
